name: Waste Connections
exchange: NYSE (also Toronto Stock Exchange and NYSE Texas)
description: Waste Connections is the third-largest solid waste company in North America. It collects garbage and recycling from homes and businesses, moves it through transfer stations, and disposes of much of it in landfills it owns. Its stated strategy is to target secondary and rural markets where it can hold exclusive franchise or municipal contracts or own the disposal site, and its segment EBITDA margin was 32.2 percent in 2025 (Canada 45 percent). It also runs a niche business treating and disposing of oil-and-gas drilling waste, whose revenue follows drilling activity, and it grows by buying local haulers (19 deals for $967 million in 2025). A Los Angeles-area landfill (Chiquita Canyon) was closed to waste on 2024-12-31 after $597 million of charges and has about 11,700 plaintiffs.

hq.note: Principal executive offices on the FY2025 10-K cover are in Woodbridge, Ontario; the 10-K gives its Secretary's address as 3 Waterway Square Place, The Woodlands, Texas, and Wikipedia lists The Woodlands, Texas as headquarters (see conflicts)

employees.note: Active employees, including 11,347 commercial truck drivers and 2,020 mechanics; 20,471 in the US and 3,743 in Canada; about 16% under collective bargaining agreements, mainly Teamsters (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Southern
businessLines.how: See the service lines below; the segment sells collection, transfer, disposal and recycling in its region under franchises, municipal contracts and open-market bids.

businessLines.name: Western
businessLines.how: See the service lines below; the segment sells collection, transfer, disposal and recycling in its region.

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $520.8M. Western's 'other segment items' were $(596.5)M in 2024, in line with the $480.8M Chiquita Canyon closure-liability charge plus the $116.1M landfill impairment (the 10-K does not tie the two lines together explicitly).

businessLines.name: Eastern
businessLines.how: See the service lines below; the segment sells collection, transfer, disposal and recycling in its region (it has the largest intercompany revenue of the six, $347.5M, meaning the most internal hand-offs between its own operations and other segments).

businessLines.name: Central
businessLines.how: See the service lines below; the segment sells collection, transfer, disposal and recycling in its region.

businessLines.name: Canada
businessLines.how: See the service lines below; the 10-K also reports E&P waste activity in the Canada segment. It is the highest-margin segment, with 14% of revenue and 19.6% of EBITDA.

businessLines.name: MidSouth
businessLines.how: See the service lines below; the segment sells collection, transfer, disposal and recycling in its region.

businessLines.name: Collection (commercial, residential, industrial roll-off)
businessLines.how: Monthly fees from households (billed by the municipality or the company under franchise), commercial customers on service contracts and roll-off customers per haul; priced for local cost inflation, and exclusive franchises and municipal contracts limit competition.
businessLines.description: Commercial $2,944.3M; residential $2,364.5M; industrial and construction roll-off $1,439.3M.

businessLines.name: Landfill disposal
businessLines.how: A per-ton tipping fee charged to its own haulers (which is eliminated as intercompany) and to third-party haulers and municipalities; owning the landfill is the vertical-integration advantage.
businessLines.description: Tipping fees at landfills: 65 owned MSW landfills plus operated ones (114 landfills owned or operated in all, including 20 E&P waste landfills and caverns and 17 non-MSW landfills).

businessLines.name: Transfer
businessLines.how: A per-ton fee for receiving, compacting and forwarding waste, charged to its own and third-party haulers.
businessLines.description: Transfer stations that consolidate loads for transport to landfills by truck, rail or barge (164 owned plus 60 operated at 2025-12-31).

businessLines.name: Recycling
businessLines.how: Sells collected recyclables to mills at commodity prices and charges processing fees to collection customers; commodity price risk is passed to customers where possible.
businessLines.description: Processing and selling cardboard, paper, plastics, glass and metals from 90 recycling operations. Separately, it has landfill gas recovery systems at 61 landfills (15 projects selling electricity to utilities, 17 selling pipeline-quality gas); the revenue line for those is not itemized in the pages read.

businessLines.name: E&P waste treatment, recovery and disposal
businessLines.how: Fees per barrel or ton of drilling waste paid by oil and gas producers, plus sales of recovered oil; volume follows drilling, completion and production activity in each basin.
businessLines.description: Non-hazardous oil-and-gas drilling waste (cuttings, flowback, produced water, contaminated soil) handled at E&P landfills, injection wells (88) and treatment/oil recovery facilities (36) in several US and Canadian basins.

businessLines.name: Intermodal and other
businessLines.how: Fees for moving cargo and waste containers by rail and truck.
businessLines.description: Intermodal container moves in the Pacific Northwest (four operations) and other services.

brands.name: Waste Connections
brands.share: 100% of revenue; operates in 46 US states and six Canadian provinces

brands.name: Facilities owned at 2025-12-31
brands.share: 371 collection operations; 164 transfer stations; 65 MSW landfills; 20 E&P waste landfills and caverns; 17 non-MSW landfills; 90 recycling operations; 4 intermodal operations; 88 E&P injection wells; 36 E&P treatment and oil recovery facilities (and operates 60 more transfer stations and 12 more MSW landfills it does not own)
